summary: Quiet-ish day for Solflare Packs: a few organic shout-outs (@hyperstrike's 'Just RIP @solflare packs', @AiFlippa teasing BlockRips x Solflare packs), plus one reply saying the demo is fun but real packs cost real money. The big story is still Crypto.com Rips: lots of people claiming free packs, but also complaints about lag, duplicate cards, no shipping option for some, and card payment not working. A post claims Coinbase Collect is powered by Collector Crypt (unverified). On the mainstream side, scalpers and sold-out shelves are still the top pain, and PSA opened EU grading in Frankfurt from €34.99 a card.

top_posts.why_it_matters: Organic Solflare Packs shout-out from a 6.5k-follower account. Easy reshare or reply.

top_posts.text: Crypto.com Rips: Rip It, Flip It — But Who Actually Profits? Crypto.com launched Rips on 9 November 2026, inside its main app. You buy a digital pack, open it, and reveal a real physical trading card — Pokémon, MLB, NBA, or NFL. Then you have two days...

sources_note: X search via the x connector, posts from 2026-11-12 09:10 UTC to 2026-11-13 ~09:10 UTC, 11 searches. Engagement numbers are as returned by the X API at scan time. Sales and revenue figures are what the cited accounts posted, not verified; the Coinbase Collect / Collector Crypt link is a single unconfirmed claim. Most @solflare mentions today were about the Solflare card and Breakpoint privacy teases, not Packs, so they're left out. The @danieldelophem post is a Nomu merch partnership, not Packs. Referral-code spam (Crown Cards, Drip), memecoin shilling, carding spam and giveaways were skipped. Creators already in collector-base.csv or earlier daily files were excluded.
